newsitem.title: UK: Pearson confident of Penguin provision.
newsitem.headline: Pearson confident of Penguin provision.

text.p: UK media group Pearson Plc said on Thursday it was confident that its proposals to take a charge against its 1996 profits would fully cover improper accounting discovered at its Penguin USA books unit.
A Pearson spokesman said the problem, which may lead to a charge against profits of as much as 100 million stg, had stemmed from "a very determined individual".

"We are confident we have provided for not only what we have discovered so far but also what will be discovered (as the investigation continues to its conclusion)," the spokesman said, describing likely provisions as conservative.

The improper accounting arose from unauthorised discounting of invoices for early payment by customers, leaving a discrepancy which the complex nature of Penguin's accounting, with hundreds of thousands of transactions passing through the New-York based unit's New Jersey facility, made it easier for a "very determined individual" to conceal.
"I think we are dealing with a very determined individual," the spokesman said.
Pearson said earlier in a statement that those found to be responsible for the problem, which only emerged very recently, "have been and will be appropriately dealt with", without giving details.
Pearson is due to report its 1996 results on March 18.
